title: RMIT Student Welfare Advisors
summary: Welfare Advisors provide short-term assistance navigating university processes and can connect students with appropriate RMIT or external services. They do not themselves deliver psychological counselling.
eligibility: Available to eligible students enrolled at RMIT Australia, RMIT UP and RMIT Online, excluding single-subject RMIT Online students.
contact: Book through Student Connect / Student Welfare; Student Connect phone +61 3 9925 5000, select Student Support.

title: RMIT Counselling and Psychological Services
summary: Free confidential short-term counselling for stress, anxiety, low mood and study pressure. This is routine support, not an emergency service.
eligibility: Current RMIT University students located in Australia. RMIT UP students should use the separate RMIT UP counselling pathway published on the RMIT UP Student Wellbeing page.
contact: Book through the official counselling page / Student Connect portal.

title: RMIT UP Student Wellbeing and counselling
summary: RMIT UP provides a separate counselling contact. Appointments may be by phone, video or in person during published weekday availability.
eligibility: Free and confidential counselling is published for RMIT UP international students studying in Foundation Studies, Fast Track and English Language program courses.
contact: Email wellbeing@rmit.edu.au or call (03) 9925 8172; see the official page for current appointment details.

title: RMIT Urgent Mental Health Support
summary: The official RMIT urgent mental-health support route is available by telephone or text around the clock. For immediate danger call 000.
eligibility: Published urgent support route for RMIT students in Australia; confirm location if the student is overseas.

title: RMIT Student Connect
summary: Official first-contact enquiries and appointment navigation, including wellbeing, support and housing.
eligibility: RMIT students; students in specialist programs should check their dedicated pathway.
contact: Official web portal and support channels; phone +61 3 9925 5000. Check current hours on source.

title: RMIT Safer Community
summary: Safer Community can respond to threatening, unwanted or concerning behaviour and refer students to other support.
eligibility: RMIT community members; check official page for the relevant reporting pathway.

title: Monash Counselling
summary: Monash offers free confidential counselling in person or by telehealth for university students.
eligibility: Monash University students. This record does not establish Monash College eligibility; Monash College students should use or confirm their own dedicated support pathway.
contact: Appointments: (03) 9905 3020. Weekday office hours on source page.

title: Monash 24/7 phone counselling
summary: Monash publishes round-the-clock phone counselling access for students.
eligibility: Monash University students. Check the source page for overseas access numbers.

title: Monash Safer Community Unit
summary: Responds to reports and disclosures of concerning, threatening and inappropriate behaviour. Offers reporting and support navigation information.
eligibility: Monash students and staff; confirm service scope using the official page.

title: University of Melbourne CAPS counselling
summary: Free confidential short-term individual psychological counselling and related support for eligible students.
eligibility: Currently enrolled University of Melbourne students located in Australia. Students offshore must check the university’s separate guidance.
contact: Appointments via the official CAPS page; phone +61 3 8344 6927.

title: University of Melbourne CAPS wellbeing workshops
summary: CAPS offers free webinars, workshops and group programs on mental health, personal development and wellbeing.
eligibility: Check individual program availability, enrollment/registration and current dates on the official page.
contact: View the workshops page; enquiries: caps-workshops@unimelb.edu.au.

title: University of Melbourne Mental Health Crisis Support Service
summary: The university provides a 24/7 mental-health crisis support service for immediate advice and information about next steps. It is not ongoing counselling. In immediate danger call 000.
eligibility: University of Melbourne students seeking 24/7 mental-health support and advice. In immediate danger, call 000; the service is not ongoing counselling.

title: eSafety tertiary-student online safety resources
summary: The Australian eSafety Commissioner provides tertiary-student resources on understanding online harm and where to find help. Different formal report categories have different eligibility criteria.
eligibility: General education resources for tertiary students; do not assume eligibility for a specific reporting scheme.
contact: Read the official student guidance and reporting links.

title: eSafety adult cyber abuse reporting
summary: Provides steps and reporting information for severe online abuse. Report the content to the platform first and consult the published reporting threshold and steps.
eligibility: The formal scheme concerns people ordinarily living in Australia aged 18 or older and subject to the defined serious-abuse threshold. A general upsetting post does not automatically qualify.
contact: Review reporting criteria on the official page and follow its reporting instructions.

title: Lifeline Australia
summary: Lifeline offers confidential crisis support through trained human supporters. Immediate danger requires 000.
eligibility: Australia-wide crisis support by phone, text and chat. If life is in danger, call 000.
